subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw accept `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` as a public model compat key and default it on for DeepSeek/Xiaomi, or choose the open config-free suffix-relocation strategy instead?
rationale: Both approaches target the same costly provider-cache regression, but adding a compat/default surface is a compatibility-sensitive provider policy decision that code inspection alone should not settle.

options.title: Accept this compat/default strategy
options.body: Merge this PR after normal maintainer review and treat the new compat key plus DeepSeek/Xiaomi defaults as the provider-cache mitigation.

options.title: Narrow the provider defaults
options.body: Keep the compat key but default only the live-proven DeepSeek path, leaving Xiaomi opt-in until provider-specific proof exists.

options.title: Prefer the config-free sibling
options.body: Pause or close this PR only if maintainers choose https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94945 and it becomes a viable proof-positive landing path.

recommendation.title: Accept this compat/default strategy
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after normal maintainer review and treat the new compat key plus DeepSeek/Xiaomi defaults as the provider-cache mitigation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest history signal for the boundary-aware transport behavior and is listed for Agents ownership in CONTRIBUTING.md.
